messages.author: 59e7d8d24bd426b2
messages.subject: calculate values relative to subset
parts:
Hi, 

I need to compute the  value of a number of parameters relative to a subset of the whole set of data. Thus, I want to divide some variables by the mean of a subset of them.
I came out with the following expression, but I can’t find a way to introduce a filter as the argument to mean().

S%>%select (Num, DiskRad:Occup)%>%
  mutate_each(funs (ratio= ./mean(.)), Num, DiskRad:Occup)

I also tried to calculate the vector of mean values separately and do

S%>%select (Num, DiskRad:Occup)%>%
  mutate_each(funs (ratio= ./the_means), Num, DiskRad:Occup)

Anyone would have a suggestion ? I’m sure I’m missing something simple here…

Thanks in advance !

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: calculate values relative to subset
parts:
Alain, 

Can you supply some toy data to play with? 

It looks to me like you're missing a group_by() to subset your data (S) by and then apply the function within. I'm also unsure why you are using select and then telling mutate_each() the same columns. I think you probably only need one or the other (although that shouldn't actually cause an issue AFAIK). 

B

messages.subject: Re: calculate values relative to subset
parts:
Just to clarify. In your first example, it looked like you wanted to divide by the mean of the group. 

For Group A, A[1]/mean[groupA], A[2]/mean(groupA), ... 
For Group B, B[1]/mean[groupB], B[2]/mean(groupB), ... 
...

Which, I think works if you do this:
S%>%group_by(Group)%>% mutate_each(funs(ratio= ./mean(.)))


Now you are saying you'd like to divide everything by the mean of group B? 
Like this?
For Group A, A[1]/mean[groupB], A[2]/mean(groupB), ... 
...

I'll have to think harder about this one. Might be easier to safe mean(groupB) as a new variable and use that in the computation. 

B

messages.subject: Re: calculate values relative to subset
parts:
Here are two solutions. One does not use  join, the other does. Hadley, is this what you had in mind ?

Both seem convoluted, to me at least. 

I think the underlying question was whether it is possible to apply transformations to series of variables that are not unary functions like mean(x) but binary like ratio(x, y) ?

# Example data

S <- data_frame(Group = rep( letters[1:3], 10),
    X = rep( c( 10, 20, 40), 10) + rnorm( 30, 0, 1),

Y = rep( c( 10, 30, 90), 10) + rnorm( 30, 0, 1),
    Z = rep( c(10, 40, 160), 10) +rnorm(30, 0, 1) )

# This does not work
S <- cbind(S, filter(S, Group=="b")%>%summarise_each(funs(mean), M=X:Z)) %>% mutate_each(funs(ratio=./(M1:M3)), X:Z)

# Group means : absolute values
group_by(S, Group)%>% summarise_each(funs(mean), X:Z)

# Do the transformation
S1 <- cbind(S, filter(S, Group=="b”) %>% 
summarise_each(funs(mean), M=X:Z)) %>% 
  mutate (X=X/M1, Y=Y/M2, Z=Z/M3) %>% 
select(Group:Z)

# Group means : relative to Group B
group_by(S1, Group)%>% summarise_each(funs(mean), X:Z)

# Other solution with join --
SLong <- S %>% gather(Var, Val, -Group) 
SLong  <- SLong %>% filter(Group=="b") %>% 
group_by(Var)%>% 
summarize(Mean=mean(Val)) %>%
left_join(SLong,., by="Var") %>% 
mutate(RelVal=Val/Mean) %>% 
select(Group, Var, RelVal)
